who: Thad W. Tate, historian of colonial Virginia at William & Mary, PhD Brown 1960.

evidence.says: William & Mary's finding aid identifies Thad W. Tate as a colonial Virginia historian who earned his Brown PhD in 1960 and joined its history faculty.
The department newsletter says Lynn Nelson's dissertation on the Tye River Valley, 1730–1860, was completed under Thad Tate's direction.
The authority identifies Thad W. Tate as professor of history at William & Mary and director of the Institute of Early American History and Culture.

notes: Exact doctorate match, institutional match, and direct corroboration of Nelson's supervision.

who: Joseph E. Taylor III, environmental and western North American historian at Simon Fraser, formerly Iowa State; PhD Washington 1996.

evidence.says: Taylor's institutional vita lists a Washington history PhD in 1996, Iowa State history appointments in 1996–2003, and Simon Fraser employment beginning in 2004.
The authority for Joseph E. Taylor III identifies the author of Making Salmon, with degrees from Oregon and Washington, seven years at Iowa State, and Simon Fraser employment since 2004.

notes: The doctorate and both universities agree; the Iowa State appointment precedes Orth's 2004 completion.

who: Victoria Elizabeth Thompson, historian of France at Arizona State during the listed dissertations, subsequently Georgia Tech.

evidence.says: ASU explicitly lists Victoria Thompson as advisor of Linnea Caproni's 2017 Casas Montezumas dissertation and Benjamin Hruska's 2012 Baptized by Saltwater dissertation.

The authority connects Victoria Elizabeth Thompson, Victoria Thompson, and Victoria E. Thompson; it cites the 1993 Gender, Class and the Marketplace dissertation and identifies her as an ASU history professor.
Georgia Tech identifies Thompson as a historian of eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Paris who joined in 2023 after 24 years at Arizona State.
The alternative Victor D. Thompson is a University of Georgia scholar with a Kentucky anthropology PhD in 2006.

notes: Both named students are directly confirmed. Victor D. Thompson (p-104190) is a different scholar.

who: Robert W. Thurston, historian of Russia and mass persecution at Miami University, PhD Michigan 1980.

evidence.says: Miami's history department lists Robert Thurston as professor emeritus, with a Michigan PhD in 1980, research interests including Russia, and Life and Terror in Stalin's Russia among his publications.
The authority identifies Robert W. Thurston, also Robert William Thurston, as the historian responsible for Life and Terror in Stalin's Russia and Liberal City, Conservative State.

notes: The Michigan doctorate matches exactly; the authority and Miami profile share the same historical works.

who: Dennis Nodín Valdés, also Dionicio Nodín Valdés, historian at Minnesota and Michigan State, PhD Michigan 1978.

evidence.says: The 1999 author biography identifies Dennis Nódin Valdés as a Minnesota associate professor teaching in History and Chicano Studies, with a Michigan history doctorate in 1978.

The authority connects Dennis Nodín Valdés with Dionicio Nodín Valdés, identifies his Minnesota appointment, and cites a 2005 biography describing him as a history professor and senior researcher at Michigan State.

notes: The doctorate and both institutions agree. The authority explicitly connects the Dennis and Dionicio name forms.

who: Wendy L. Wall, historian of twentieth-century United States political culture at Binghamton, PhD Stanford 1998.

evidence.says: Wall's CV lists a Stanford history PhD in 1998, Binghamton employment beginning in September 2010, earlier Colgate employment in 2000–2008, and Inventing the American Way.
The authority connects Wendy Wall with Wendy L. Wall, author of Inventing the American Way, and records a Stanford PhD in 1998 and the Colgate history appointment.

notes: The authority's earlier Colgate affiliation and the CV's later Binghamton appointment describe the same career; Binghamton dates cover both students.

who: Rachel Judith Weil, historian of early modern English political and cultural history at Cornell, PhD Princeton 1991.

evidence.says: Cornell identifies Rachel Judith Weil as a history professor researching early modern England, and names Political Passions and A Plague of Informers as her books.
The Institute for Advanced Study lists Rachel Weil's Princeton PhD in 1991, links her Cornell faculty page, and explicitly supplies ORCID 0000-0002-0254-8630.
The authority connects Rachel Judith Weil and Rachel Weil through the 1991 dissertation Sexual Ideology and Political Propaganda, Political Passions, and A Plague of Informers.

notes: Both candidates represent this supervisor: p-11304's ORCID is directly linked to Cornell by IAS. Selected the fuller authority-linked record p-120777; p-11304 is a duplicate candidate.

who: Elizabeth Ann Williams, historian of medicine at Oklahoma State, PhD Indiana.

evidence.says: Oklahoma State's 2001–2002 graduate faculty list names Elizabeth A. Williams as associate professor of history with a PhD from Indiana University.
The history department lists Elizabeth A. Williams among its emeriti faculty as professor emerita.
The authority expands Elizabeth A. Williams to Elizabeth Ann Williams and identifies the Oklahoma State medical historian and author of The Physical and the Moral.

notes: The authority, history appointment, and Indiana doctorate identify the matching candidate. The doctorate year was not independently verified.
